{{short description|German vertebrate paleontologist and developmental biologist}}
'''Nadia Belinda Fröbisch''' (née Stöcker) is a German vertebrate paleontologist and developmental biologist who specializes in the evolution and development of amphibians. She is currently a professor at the [[Natural History Museum, Berlin|Museum für Naturkunde Berlin]] in the Leibniz Institute for Research on Evolution and Biodiversity.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=Prof. Nadia Fröbisch, Ph.D.|url=https://www.museumfuernaturkunde.berlin/en/about/team/nadia.froebisch|website=}}</ref>

== Academic and professional background ==
Fröbisch obtained her [[vordiplom]] (B.Sc. equivalent) at the [[University of Bonn]] in Germany (1996-1999), after which she spent a year as a visiting student at the [[University of Calgary]] and volunteered at the [[Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology|Royal Tyrell Museum]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=2006 (Romer Prize) - Nadia Fröbisch|url=http://vertpaleo.org/the-Society/Awards/Past-Award-Winners/2006-(Romer-Prize)-Nadia-Frobisch.aspx|website=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=Nadia Stoecker CV|url=http://redpath-staff.mcgill.ca/larsson/personalpages/nadia_froebisch/nadia_froebisch_cv.pdf|website=}}</ref> Following that, she pursued her diploma (M.Sc. equivalent) at the University of Bonn (2000-2003) under the supervision of Martin Sander, where she studied [[Middle Triassic]] [[Ichthyosauria|ichthyosaur]]s. Fröbisch then went on to pursue her doctoral studies at [[McGill University]] (2003-2008) under the supervision of Robert Carroll and Hans Larsson, where she studied the extinct [[Dissorophoidea|dissorophoid]] [[Temnospondyli|temnospondyls]], a close relative of modern amphibians.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Fröbisch|first=Nadia|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/30003398|title=Ontogeny and phylogeny of small dissorophoid amphibians|publisher=McGill University|year=2008|isbn=|location=Montreal|pages=1–360}}</ref> She went on to hold postdoctoral positions at the [[University of Toronto Mississauga]] (supervised by [[Robert R. Reisz|Robert Reisz]]) and the University of Chicago (supervised by [[Neil Shubin]]). She is currently a professor at the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin and is technically affiliated with [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin - Professorin N. Fröbisch|url=https://agnes.hu-berlin.de/lupo/rds;jsessionid=2C39B344344E82AECCF4CCA1A32DF5F6.angua_root?state=verpublish&status=init&vmfile=no&moduleCall=webInfo&publishConfFile=webInfoPerson&publishSubDir=personal&keep=y&purge=y&personal.pid=26396|access-date=2021-01-02|website=agnes.hu-berlin.de}}</ref>

She won the Canadian Paleontology Conference's Bolton Award in 2006, given to the best student presentation, and the [[Society of Vertebrate Paleontology]]'s Romer Prize in 2006, a prestigious award given for the best student talk based on doctoral research.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=SVP - Past Award Winners|url=http://vertpaleo.org/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190317023907/http://vertpaleo.org/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.aspx|archive-date=2019-03-17|website=}}</ref> She appeared in an episode of [[National Geographic Society|National Geographic's]] TV series "[[Naked Science]]"<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=Nadia Fröbisch|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4205593/|website=[[IMDb]]}}</ref> and was a Society of Vertebrate Paleontology Distinguished Lecturer from 2018 to 2020; this program was originally an initiative of the [[Paleontological Society]] to make accomplished scientists available for public lectures.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=Distinguished Lecture Program|url=https://www.paleosoc.org/distinguished-lecturer-program|website=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=SVP/Paleo Society Distinguished Lecturer Program|url=http://vertpaleo.org/What-is-Vertebrate-Paleontology/SVP-Paleo-Society-Distinguished-Lecturer-Program.aspx|website=}}</ref>

== Academic contributions ==
Fröbisch's research focuses primarily on the evolution and development of extinct and extant amphibians through the combined use of paleontological and modern developmental approaches. In particular, she is well known for her work examining patterns of limb development<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fröbisch|first1=Nadia B.|last2=Carroll|first2=Robert L.|last3=Schoch|first3=Rainer R.|date=2007-01-12|title=Limb ossification in the Paleozoic branchiosaurid Apateon (Temnospondyli) and the early evolution of preaxial dominance in tetrapod limb development|journal=Evolution & Development|volume=9|issue=1|pages=69–75|doi=10.1111/j.1525-142x.2006.00138.x|pmid=17227367|s2cid=10644859|issn=1520-541X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fröbisch|first1=Nadia B.|last2=Shubin|first2=Neil H.|date=2011-04-04|title=Salamander limb development: Integrating genes, morphology, and fossils|journal=Developmental Dynamics|volume=240|issue=5|pages=1087–1099|doi=10.1002/dvdy.22629|pmid=21465623|issn=1058-8388|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Fröbisch|first=Nadia Reviews|volume=83|issue=4|pages=571–600|doi=10.1111/j.1469-185x.2008.00055.x|pmid=18947337|s2cid=9148543|issn=1464-7931}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fröbisch|first1=Nadia Biology|language=en|volume=21|issue=4|pages=424–431|doi=10.1016/j.semcdb.2009.11.001|pmid=19913630}}</ref> and regeneration.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fröbisch|first1=Nadia She also serves on the editorial board of several paleontological journals, including [[PalZ]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=PalZ - Editors|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/12542/editors|website=}}</ref> the Journal of Paleontology,<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=Journal of Paleontology - Editorial Board|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-paleontology/information/editorial-board|website=}}</ref> and Paleobiology.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-12-23|title=Paleobiology - Editorial Board|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/paleobiology/information/editorial-board|website=}}</ref>
